MLforSEO Academy · The AI-powered Entity Audit

Knowledge Graph Reconciler

Match your extracted entities against Google's Knowledge Graph, and flag the ones where the returned type contradicts the type your content implies.

What you need
The same Google key, with the Knowledge Graph Search API also enabled
Cost
Free — 100,000 lookups a day
Feed it
entity_mentions.csv from the Extractor, or a pasted list
You get back
kg_reconciliation.csv — matched, ambiguous, unmatched, with type conflicts flagged

How to use it

  1. Paste your key and upload the entity export.
  2. Leave the match-score floor at 20 unless you have a reason to change it.
  3. Read the three verdicts before you read a single row.
  4. Filter to type conflicts — those are matches that are confidently wrong.
  5. Export, and keep the file for the Scorecard.

Worth knowing. A returned match is not a correct match. Check the type and the description before you trust the score.

Knowledge Graph Reconciler

Match your extracted entities to Google’s Knowledge Graph, and find the three ways it goes wrong: no match at all, an ambiguous match, or a confident match to the wrong thing.

1 · Your API key

Held in this tab only. 100,000 lookups a day are free.
The Knowledge Graph Search API is a legacy service. Google directs new projects to Cloud Enterprise Knowledge Graph and warns it is “not suitable for use as a production-critical service”. Fine for auditing; do not build a live product on it.

2 · Your entities

Paste one entity per line, or upload the entity_mentions.csv from the Entity Extractor — that adds NLP types and MIDs, which unlocks type-conflict and over-linking detection.
Or paste below.
Add a key and some entities to begin.
Reading resultScore correctly: it is a relevance score for this lookup — how well the entity name matched a graph node. It is not authority, not popularity, and not a ranking signal. A high score means “confident match”, nothing more.

Reconciliation

Suspected over-linking

Same MID, divergent wording
These entities were given the same Knowledge Graph MID by the NLP API despite describing different things. An over-linked entity is worse than an unlinked one: you are actively teaching machines that your thing is something else.
